headline: Sell New Orleans first and the Pelicans second: hand-made city craft timed to king cake, second lines and crawfish.
thesis: New Orleans fans wear the city before the team: Dirty Coast and Fleurty Girl phrase tees, ward numbers and school colors beat a Pelicans logo that only dates to 2013, in a town that has watched the Jazz leave and the Hornets spend two Katrina seasons in Oklahoma City. The city runs on its own clock (second-line Sundays from Labor Day to June, king cake from Jan 6 to Mardi Gras on Feb 9, 2027, crawfish through Jazz Fest), and that clock overlaps the NBA season almost exactly. After a 26-56 season, with first-year coach Jamahl Mosley and no 2026 first-round pick, standings won't sell product here; craft and calendar will. Nike wins by commissioning the city's hands (sign painters, brass bands, Social Aid & Pleasure Clubs, bounce artists), paying them, and dropping product on New Orleans dates rather than league dates.

archetype.name: The Second Line
archetype.description: They dance behind the city's main line (Saints, LSU and Carnival), loyal through every relocation scare and loud when the music is right. They buy city pride first and team gear second, and they punish anything that reads tourist.

pulse.teamMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout scorer Trey Murphy III (21.5 ppg, kept through June trade rumors) and young Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears after a 26-56 season and a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars. The team is not on the opening-night or Christmas slates; NBA Cup West Group B (OKC, MIN, LAC, MEM) is the early-season stage.
pulse.sentiment: Weary, not angry: protective of Murphy, hopeful on Queen and Fears, cautious about building anything on Zion's availability, and still more excited by the City Edition than by the roster.

topInsights.title: City mark first, team mark second
topInsights.insight: Locals put local phrase tees over team gear, and the Pelicans compete with Saints black-and-gold and LSU purple-and-gold for the same shirt drawer. The 2023-24 City Edition, the one the team brought back in 2025-26, proved that local storytelling is what this fan base rewards.
topInsights.implication: Make every hero piece pass as New Orleans pride on the street, with the Pelicans mark as a secondary lockup, a jock tag or a sleeve hit rather than the chest graphic.

topInsights.title: The NBA season is second-line season
topInsights.insight: Social Aid & Pleasure Clubs parade most Sundays from Labor Day into June in new color-matched suits and fresh sneakers, the city's living fashion show, and their colors stay secret until parade day. No other NBA market has a weekly street-style ritual on the same calendar as its home schedule.
topInsights.implication: Build tonal, color-matchable sneaker and warm-up sets, commission one club per season as a paid co-designer, and copy their rollout: reveal on the day, never leak-then-drop.

topInsights.title: The Carnival palette is spent; the city's craft isn't
topInsights.insight: Purple, green and gold is already on the fan-favorite City Edition and on every souvenir in the Quarter. What locals haven't seen on a jersey is the hand-made city: blue-and-white tile street names, sign painters' dot-bordered lettering, iron lace, brass-band drum heads and doubloons.
topInsights.implication: Use commissioned craft (tile numerals, hand-lettered alphabets, iron-lace jacquard, brushed-brass hardware) as the design system, and keep Carnival color to January accents.

topInsights.title: Food is the most precise retail clock
topInsights.insight: Attention for the Pelicans peaks October to December, and then the city's own seasons take over: king cake from Jan 6 to Feb 9, crawfish and Lenten fish fries from March to May, sno-balls all summer. The Pelicans already own the best inside joke of the season, the King Cake Baby.
topInsights.implication: Sequence drops by what's on the table: king cake knit on Jan 6, a crawfish-red stretch-run pack in March, nectar-cream pink for spring and summer. Never launch a hero drop in the final two weeks before Mardi Gras.

topInsights.title: Identity is ward, school and side of the river
topInsights.insight: New Orleanians place each other by high school ('What school you went to?') and by ward, which bounce records shout out by number, while the West Bank and New Orleans East rep separately. School programs like St. Aug and Edna Karr carry more block-level loyalty than a losing pro team.
topInsights.implication: Build modular identity product (ward numerals, East and West Bank pieces, licensed school co-brands) so fans wear their exact New Orleans, drawn by artists from each area.

topInsights.title: Permanence beats promises
topInsights.insight: Basketball has left New Orleans twice and relocation chatter returns in seasons like 26-56, so fans trust things that root the team in place. Murphy is the player fans trust, Zion is the brand (and a Jordan Brand athlete), and the pelican itself, back from zero after DDT, is a comeback story nobody has put on product.
topInsights.implication: Tell 'still here' stories (pelican in her piety liners, school and ward ties) instead of contention messaging, and spread player product across Murphy, Queen and Fears so the line doesn't depend on one availability report.

topInsights.title: The sacred line is also the market's credibility test
topInsights.insight: Black Masking Indian suits, chants and patches are sacred and individually authored, second-line regalia belongs to its clubs, and bounce was built by queer Black artists. This city has already beaten the NFL once, over the 'Who Dat' letters in 2010, and it calls out brands that borrow without paying.
topInsights.implication: Pay up front and give credit by name (parade fees, instrument donations, royalties), never print or trace Indian beadwork, and let culture bearers like the Backstreet Cultural Museum set the terms before any outreach.

opportunities.title: Twelfth Night Pack
opportunities.summary: The season's biggest city-specific drop, released on Jan 6 when king cake season and Carnival begin, built on sanding-sugar texture and the team-owned King Cake Baby rather than beads and masks.
where: Pelicans Team Store, Smoothie King Center
Dong Phuong Bakery, New Orleans East
Dirty Coast and Fleurty Girl, Magazine Street
opportunities.when: Jan 6 launch through Mardi Gras Day (Feb 9, 2027); restock by mid-January, with no new hero launch after about Jan 26
opportunities.how: Sell the pack in a king-cake-style box next to a paid, co-branded cake from Dong Phuong. Hide the King Cake Baby on a waistband tab ('got the baby' wins a lagniappe item), and run a Carnival-season home night with the mascot.
opportunities.segment: Diehard locals, families and Carnival visitors
opportunities.kpi: Sell-through above 70% by Feb 1 and share of January Pelicans revenue versus January 2026

opportunities.title: Ward Call and 'What School You Went To?'
opportunities.summary: A modular identity line: tile-set ward numerals, West Bank and The East pieces, and licensed co-brands with New Orleans high school programs, each drawn by an artist from that area.
where: High school gyms (St. Aug, Edna Karr, Warren Easton, McDonogh 35)
opportunities.when: Launch at a home game in late October, then run ward-themed home nights through the All-Star break
opportunities.how: Launch with a bounce call-and-response set ('Where dey at?' answered ward by ward) led by Big Freedia and credited queer bounce artists. Pay one artist per ward, and send school-pack proceeds and gear back to each school's team.
opportunities.segment: Neighborhood locals, high school families and young hoopers
opportunities.kpi: Units by ward and school code, share sold outside Orleans Parish core doors, and repeat buyers across two or more wards

opportunities.title: Still Here holiday core
opportunities.summary: Capture the year's peak attention (November Cup nights through December) with accessible player and kids product spread across Murphy, Queen, Fears and Zion, plus 'still here' story pieces.
opportunities.when: Cup Friday nights Oct 30 to Nov 27, Black Friday, and through December
opportunities.how: Bundle a kids swingman with a tee at a value price for local households, and run Cup-night giveaways with a Memphis rivalry graphic for the Grizzlies game. Add a navy warm-up with a pelican-in-her-piety liner that explains the name.
products: Kids swingman jerseys (Murphy, Queen, Fears, Zion)
opportunities.segment: Families, gift buyers and Gulf South regional fans
opportunities.kpi: Holiday units versus 2025, kids share of jersey sales, and the share of player units that are not Zion

opportunities.title: Second Line Sunday club commission
opportunities.summary: Each season one Social Aid & Pleasure Club co-designs a tonal sneaker colorway and a satin-trimmed warm-up in its own colors, released after its parade and credited by name.
where: Pelicans Team Store, Sunday home games
opportunities.when: Commission at the start of second-line season; release the week after the club's parade, before a Sunday home game
opportunities.how: Approach through culture bearers such as the Backstreet Cultural Museum, then pay the club and its brass band and underwrite its parade permit and police fees. The club picks the colors and approves everything, and the swoosh never touches its regalia.
products: Matched tee, short and cap set
opportunities.segment: Second-line culture and style-led Black New Orleanians
opportunities.kpi: Sell-out time, the club's public endorsement, and whether a second club asks to be next season's partner

opportunities.title: Brass series and Bayou Classic band warm-up
opportunities.summary: Treat Pelicans Gold as sousaphone brass: foil, hardware and drum-head lettering credited to a named brass band, plus a frogging-trimmed band warm-up for Bayou Classic weekend.
where: Pelicans Team Store, Smoothie King Center
Caesars Superdome footprint, Bayou Classic weekend
Maple Leaf Bar and Tipitina's (launch events)
opportunities.when: Bayou Classic weekend (Nov 27-28, 2026), with a second wave in Mardi Gras week
opportunities.how: Lead the launch with Rebirth Brass Band and pair each drop with an instrument donation through the Tipitina's Foundation or The Roots of Music. Co-create the band warm-up with St. Augustine's Marching 100 and pay the program back in uniforms or instruments.
opportunities.segment: HBCU and band-culture fans, Bayou Classic visitors and music-first locals
opportunities.kpi: Bayou Classic weekend sell-through, visitor versus local zip-code split, and instruments funded

opportunities.title: Boil Season and Nectar Cream
opportunities.summary: Give the stretch run and summer their own palette (boiled-crawfish red, nectar-cream pink, seersucker) in heat-ready mesh, instead of reusing Carnival colors.
where: Riverwalk Outlets and Canal Place (Jazz Fest visitors)
opportunities.when: Mid-March (Lent and crawfish season) through French Quarter Fest and Jazz Fest, then summer
opportunities.how: Launch Boil Season for the stretch run and any Play-In push (Apr 13-16), then switch to Nectar Cream with a paid sno-ball stand collab. Drop a commissioned poster-style tee from a Black New Orleans artist in the Jazz Fest window, with no festival marks.
opportunities.segment: Locals in festival season and spring visitors
opportunities.kpi: March-to-May Pelicans apparel revenue versus 2026 and visitor sell-through at downtown doors

opportunities.title: Claiborne Oaks at Essence
opportunities.summary: A Black New Orleans artist capsule in which a commissioned painter paints the live oaks the I-10 overpass erased back onto wraparound panels, launched for the national audience at Essence Festival.
where: Smoothie King Center and Superdome area, Essence weekend
Ashé Cultural Arts Center, Central City
opportunities.when: Essence Festival of Culture, July 4 weekend 2027
opportunities.how: Commission BMike Odums or artists in the Willie Birch lineage for original work, not reproductions of existing murals. Send proceeds to a Claiborne Corridor group the artists choose, and keep everything away from Aug 29.
products: Premium hoodie with oak side panels
opportunities.segment: The national Black audience at Essence and culture-led locals
opportunities.kpi: Essence-weekend revenue, out-of-state share of buyers, and dollars returned to the corridor

collection.name: Made by Hand
collection.story: New Orleans marks its own identity by hand: tiles at every street corner, sign painters' glitter, sousaphone brass, king cake sugar and the crawfish table. This collection is built by the people who make those things, credited and paid, so a Pelicans fan wears the city's own handwriting instead of a souvenir.

themes.name: Corner Tile
themes.story: Every New Orleanian knows their corner by its blue-and-white tile street name; this theme sets wards, neighborhoods and numbers in that tile grid.
themes.graphics: Square-tile block capitals with a tile border for TREMÉ, 7TH WARD, WESTBANK and THE EAST, plus a crescent-and-star water-meter roundel as a quiet secondary mark.
themes.materials: Heavyweight cotton jersey with a glazed-look high-density print, debossed rubber crescent-and-star patches, and Dri-FIT mesh for the shooting shirts.

pieces.detail: One ward per tee in tile type, drawn with an artist from that ward.
Short-sleeve mesh with tile-grid numbers and a tile-border hem.
A youth cut with the neighborhood name and a hidden pelican tile.
Debossed water-meter roundel on the front, ward number on the side.

themes.name: Brass and Iron
themes.story: Pelicans Gold already reads as a tarnished sousaphone bell; this theme pairs brass-band hardware and drum-head lettering with original iron-lace patterning.
themes.segment: Music-first locals, band culture and premium buyers
themes.graphics: Circular drum-head lockups lettered by a New Orleans sign painter, and an original iron-lace railing drawing with a hidden 'NO' monogram.
themes.materials: Brushed-brass zipper pulls, aglets and snaps, laser-cut iron-lace perforations, tonal jacquard knit, and satin taping for the Sunday pieces.

pieces.detail: Laser-cut lace panels at the yoke with brushed-brass hardware.
A credited brass band's name arched over a circular sign-painted lockup.
Pelicans Gold foil wordmark and a brass drawcord tip.
Tonal lace side panel with the monogram in the scrollwork.
Braid and cross-belt trim co-created with a marching band program.

themes.name: Twelfth Night
themes.story: King cake sanding sugar in purple, green and gold, rendered as glittering crystals rather than flat Carnival blocks, with the King Cake Baby hidden inside.
themes.graphics: A sugar-crystal speckle print and metallic-fleck knit, two-sided doubloon jock tags with a new theme each season, and the baby on the waistband.
themes.materials: Metallic-fleck knit, speckle-print fleece, and anodized-aluminum two-sided doubloon tags.

pieces.detail: Tri-color crystal fleck on a navy ground, with the baby inside the collar.
The baby on the waistband tab and a doubloon on the leg.
Sugar-speckle print across the hood and cuffs only, with a navy body.
A numbered set of Pelicans doubloons made with a local doubloon maker.

themes.name: Boil Season
themes.story: The stretch run and summer in the colors of the newspaper-covered crawfish table and the nectar-cream sno-ball, built for 80°F festival days.
themes.segment: Festival-season locals, spring visitors and summer hoopers
themes.graphics: A newsprint-grain texture under crawfish red (with no real mastheads), hand-painted sno-ball-stand menu lettering, and navy-and-white seersucker stripes.
themes.materials: Perforated mesh, quick-dry woven, navy-and-white seersucker panels, and packable water-resistant shells.

pieces.detail: Perforated mesh with a newsprint-grain sleeve and navy numerals.
Seersucker side panels on a navy mesh body.
Pink footbed, navy strap and a hand-lettered 'nectar' hit.
Navy shell with a nectar-pink lining that packs into its own pocket.

uniform.narrative: At almost every corner in the city, the street name is set in blue-and-white tile in the sidewalk, and every New Orleanian has stood on theirs. The jersey spells NEW ORLEANS tile by tile, wraps it in an original iron-lace side panel, and puts the city's hand-made civic design on court instead of another round of Carnival color. It belongs to every ward and side of the river at once, and it is nobody's sacred property.
motifs: Square-tile block capitals set on a grid, with a tile border around the wordmark
Original iron-lace railing drawing with a hidden 'NO' monogram in the scrollwork
Pelican in her piety, the state's comeback bird, inside the collar
uniform.typography: A 'NEW ORLEANS' wordmark and numbers built square by square on a tile grid, drawn and signed by a New Orleans sign painter and lettering artist, with cobalt fills and a thin navy outline. No script and no fleur-de-lis in the wordmark.
details: Waistband: ward numerals 1 to 17 in tile type running around the band, plus WESTBANK and THE EAST
Side panel: tonal iron-lace jacquard in glazed white on white, with the monogram at hip height
Jock tag: debossed brass crescent-and-star roundel with the lettering artist's signature
Neck tape: a 'lagniappe' inner tag telling the brown pelican's return from zero
Court: tile-bordered street-name corners at each baseline, as if the court sits on a city corner
avoid: Purple, green and gold as the lead: the 2023-24 design brought back in 2025-26 already owns Carnival color
Fleur-de-lis as the hero: it reads as the Saints, and the Code Noir used it to brand enslaved people
Black Masking Indian beadwork, plumes or chief iconography in any form, and copying any club's regalia
Katrina waterlines, FEMA X-codes, voodoo and Bourbon Street or 'N'awlins' tourist shorthand
Copying a real tiled street name, a specific building's railing, or Simon's or Dr. Bob's signature styles

partners.name: Dirty Coast
partners.why: Its neighborhood in-jokes are what locals wear over team gear, which makes it the city-first voice the Pelicans lack.
partners.idea: Co-write Ward Call graphics and run a pre-cleared rapid-response tee program for big player moments.

partners.name: Fleurty Girl
partners.type: Local tee and gift brand with multiple doors
partners.why: It became the local face of the city's tee vernacular when the NFL sent its 2010 'Who Dat' letters, and it reaches local women and families.
partners.idea: Host the Twelfth Night drop in its Magazine Street and Metairie doors and co-design a family and kids Carnival tee.

partners.name: Studio BE (Brandan 'BMike' Odums)
partners.why: The city's most credible street artist, whose work paints back what was lost after Katrina and urban renewal.
partners.idea: Commission the Claiborne Oaks capsule and a signed print for Essence weekend, with proceeds to a corridor group he chooses.

partners.name: Rebirth Brass Band with the Tipitina's Foundation
partners.type: Brass band and school music nonprofit
partners.why: Rebirth is the standard every second-line band is measured against, and the foundation equips school band programs.
partners.idea: Credit Rebirth on the first brass-series drop, lead the launch with a live set, and fund instruments for every unit sold.

partners.name: Dong Phuong Bakery
partners.why: Its king cake draws lines from every corner of the metro, and it carries both the Carnival and the Tết stories.
partners.idea: Bake a paid, co-branded king cake sold with the Twelfth Night Pack, and co-host the Tết x Carnival capsule.

partners.name: Backstreet Cultural Museum
partners.type: Community-run museum of Black Masking Indian and second-line culture, Tremé
partners.why: It is the right door to knock on before any engagement with second-line clubs or Black Masking traditions.
partners.idea: Act as the paid advisor and introducer for the Second Line Sunday commission, with veto rights over anything culture-adjacent.

partners.name: Big Freedia
partners.why: The global face of a genre whose ward-by-ward call-and-response is the most local typography the city has.
partners.idea: Front the Ward Call launch with an in-arena bounce set alongside credited queer bounce pioneers, once footwear and apparel conflicts are cleared.

partners.name: Feed the Second Line and the Krewe of Red Beans
partners.type: Culture-bearer nonprofit and Lundi Gras bean-mosaic krewe
partners.why: They turn a Monday dish into costume art and send money directly to maskers, club members and musicians.
partners.idea: Make a Red Beans Monday tee for Monday home games, designed by krewe bean artists, with proceeds to Feed the Second Line.

where: Taste: Dirty Coast and Fleurty Girl on Magazine Street, St. Claude Avenue pop-ups and Studio BE, where limited drops land first.
Volume: Lakeside (Metairie) and Oakwood (Gretna) through Foot Locker, Dillard's and Dick's, where families buy kids jerseys and mainstream colorways.
Launch: the Pelicans Team Store at Smoothie King Center for City Edition, Cup nights and Twelfth Night moments.
Social and events: Instagram-driven local sellers plus Essence, Bayou Classic and Jazz Fest pop-ups for visitor spend.
when: Late October to December is peak Pelicans attention and the year's biggest gifting window.
Jan 6 to about Jan 26 for Carnival product; no hero launch in the two weeks before Mardi Gras (Feb 9).
Bayou Classic (Thanksgiving weekend) and Essence (July 4 weekend) for high-spend visitor drops.
Mid-March through Jazz Fest for a lightweight stretch-run and festival palette.
how: Put the city mark first and the team mark second, so product passes as New Orleans pride.
Tier the range: accessible swingman, kids and tee bundles for local households, and numbered city-keepsake pieces for visitors.
Design for 60-80°F parade days and air-conditioned arenas: mesh, seersucker, packable shells, and color-matchable tonal sets for second-line style.
Pay and credit every collaborator up front and send money back visibly (parade fees, instruments, corridor groups), because this market checks.

risks.risk: Cultural extraction, such as anything resembling Black Masking Indian beadwork or an unpaid second-line reference, would end Nike's credibility in the communities that set the city's style.
risks.mitigation: Route all culture-adjacent work through paid culture bearers with veto power, and keep sacred material out of every brief.

risks.risk: Zion is a Jordan Brand athlete with a long injury history, so a Zion-led line is both a brand conflict and fragile.
risks.mitigation: Spread player product across Murphy, Queen and Fears and coordinate any Zion piece with Jordan Brand.

risks.risk: Another sub-30-win season, a Murphy trade at the Feb 11 deadline, or renewed relocation chatter could crater team-gear demand.
risks.mitigation: Weight inventory toward city-first product that sells regardless of standings, keep team-branded volume lean, and pre-clear rapid-response tees.

risks.risk: Third-party IP is everywhere: Saints fleur-de-lis treatments, 'Who Dat', krewe marks, Hornets-era marks owned by Charlotte, school marks and food brands.
risks.mitigation: Use original commissioned art, clear school and partner licenses early, and never try to claim a local phrase as Nike or NBA property.

risks.risk: Hurricane season (June 1 to Nov 30) can wipe out Essence-to-opener events and shipping, and Aug 29 is a day of grief.
risks.mitigation: Hold flexible launch dates for summer and early fall, keep digital fallbacks, and schedule nothing commercial around Aug 29.

scorecard.rationale: Few NBA cities have a deeper or more design-ready local culture, and its calendar lines up with the season. But retail is thin (few destination sneaker doors, a modest arena store, a lower-income core), and Pelicans fandom is small, Saints-first and weary after 26-56. The opportunity is slightly above average only because city-first product can sell independent of the standings.
